concepts.name: Differential equation and its order
concepts.summary: Recognise an equation containing an unknown function and its derivatives and state its order and whether it is ordinary.

concepts.name: Solutions as functions
concepts.summary: Understand that a solution is a function that satisfies the equation, and check a candidate by substituting it and its derivatives.

concepts.name: General versus particular solution
concepts.summary: Explain that integration introduces arbitrary constants giving a family of solutions, and that a particular solution picks one member.

concepts.name: Initial value problem
concepts.summary: Describe how an initial condition fixes the constant and selects a single solution curve.

concepts.name: Direction field reading
concepts.summary: Interpret a slope field as showing the slope y' at each point and sketch how solution curves follow the arrows.

concepts.name: Rate-of-change modelling statements
concepts.summary: Understand that a statement like 'rate proportional to amount' translates into an equation such as dy/dt = ky.

misconceptions.text: A differential equation has one single answer number rather than a function or family of functions.
The order of a differential equation is the highest power of the unknown function or derivative rather than the highest derivative.
The arbitrary constant can be dropped because it does not affect the solution.

concepts.name: Separation of variables
concepts.summary: Solve dy/dx = f(x)g(y) by moving each variable to one side and integrating both sides.

concepts.name: Exponential growth and decay
concepts.summary: Apply y = y0 e^{kt} to population, radioactive decay and similar problems, determining k from data.

concepts.name: First-order linear form
concepts.summary: Rewrite a first-order equation into standard linear form and identify p(x) and q(x).

concepts.name: Integrating factor method
concepts.summary: Multiply by e^{∫p dx} so the left side becomes a product-rule derivative, then integrate to solve.

concepts.name: Equilibrium solutions
concepts.summary: Find constant solutions of an autonomous equation by setting y' = 0 and recognise those lost when dividing during separation.

concepts.name: Solving initial value problems
concepts.summary: Use the initial condition to find the constant in the general solution of a first-order equation.

concepts.name: Mixing tank models
concepts.summary: Set up and solve dQ/dt = rate in − rate out for a well-stirred tank with constant flows.

misconceptions.text: After separating variables you can integrate only one side and put the constant anywhere without consequence.
The integrating factor method works without first putting the equation in standard form with y' having coefficient 1.
In a mixing problem the outflow concentration equals the inflow concentration.

concepts.name: Exact equations and potential functions
concepts.summary: Test exactness with M_y = N_x and construct the potential function F whose level curves are the solutions.

concepts.name: Existence and uniqueness theorem
concepts.summary: Analyse when an IVP has a unique solution using continuity of f and ∂f/∂y, and find the interval on which it exists.

concepts.name: Characteristic equation method
concepts.summary: Solve ay'' + by' + cy = 0 using roots of the characteristic polynomial: real distinct, repeated or complex.

concepts.name: Superposition and linear independence
concepts.summary: Use the Wronskian to decide whether two solutions form a fundamental set and build the general solution from them.

concepts.name: Undetermined coefficients
concepts.summary: Find a particular solution of a nonhomogeneous equation by guessing a form based on the forcing term, adjusting for resonance with the homogeneous solution.

concepts.name: Qualitative analysis of autonomous equations
concepts.summary: Use a phase line to classify equilibria as stable, unstable or semi-stable and predict long-term behaviour.

concepts.name: Spring-mass oscillator model
concepts.summary: Relate the roots of the characteristic equation to undamped, underdamped, critically damped and overdamped motion.

misconceptions.text: Any equation M dx + N dy = 0 can be solved by integrating M with respect to x and N with respect to y and adding the results.
Every IVP has a solution defined for all x.
A repeated root of the characteristic equation gives only one solution, so the general solution has a single constant.

concepts.name: Laplace transform definition and properties
concepts.summary: Compute transforms from the integral definition and using linearity, the first shifting theorem and transforms of derivatives.

concepts.name: Solving IVPs by Laplace transform
concepts.summary: Transform an IVP into an algebraic equation in s, solve it, and invert using partial fractions and tables.

concepts.name: Discontinuous and impulsive forcing
concepts.summary: Model switched and impulsive inputs with unit step and delta functions and solve the resulting problems with transforms.

concepts.name: Convolution and transfer function
concepts.summary: Express the response of a linear system to arbitrary forcing as a convolution with the impulse response and interpret the transfer function.

concepts.name: Variation of parameters
aliases: particular solution by variation of parameters
concepts.summary: Construct a particular solution for general forcing using the Wronskian when undetermined coefficients does not apply.

concepts.name: Resonance and forced oscillation analysis
concepts.summary: Evaluate how forcing frequency and damping determine amplitude, beats, resonance and transient versus steady-state behaviour.

concepts.name: Choosing a solution method
concepts.summary: Judge which technique (separable, linear, exact, undetermined coefficients, variation of parameters, Laplace) is most efficient for a given equation and justify it.

misconceptions.text: The Laplace transform of a product of functions is the product of their transforms.
Laplace transforms only work for homogeneous equations or only for zero initial conditions.
Resonance occurs for any forcing frequency whenever damping is present, giving unbounded growth.

concepts.name: Systems of linear ODEs
concepts.summary: Evaluate solution structure of x' = Ax through eigenvalues and eigenvectors and relate it to higher-order equations.

concepts.name: Phase plane classification
concepts.summary: Judge stability and equilibrium type from trace and determinant of the system matrix.

concepts.name: Linearisation of nonlinear systems
concepts.summary: Assess local behaviour near equilibria of nonlinear systems via the Jacobian and recognise when linearisation is inconclusive.

concepts.name: Power series solutions
concepts.summary: Derive series solutions about ordinary points via recurrence relations and evaluate their radius of convergence.

concepts.name: Numerical method error analysis
concepts.summary: Evaluate the accuracy, order and stability of Euler and Runge–Kutta schemes and diagnose stiff problems.

concepts.name: Bifurcation analysis
concepts.summary: Create bifurcation diagrams showing how equilibria and their stability change with a parameter.

concepts.name: Constructing models from phenomena
concepts.summary: Design ODE models such as logistic growth with harvesting or predator-prey, justify assumptions and analyse their predictions.

misconceptions.text: Linearisation always determines the stability of a nonlinear equilibrium, including centres.
A smaller step size always makes a numerical ODE solver more accurate and stable regardless of the method.
A fitted ODE model that matches observed data is therefore a correct description of the underlying mechanism.
